### Rework jp2lam lossy rate control for perceptual, resolution-stable photographic quality

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem.encode-quality.improve-photographic-rate-control/1`

Raise jp2lam lossy photographic quality-per-byte toward JPEG XL/BPG and make a fixed quality hold constant PERCEPTUAL quality across resolutions. The local allocator work is the existing perceptually weighted PCRD (size-matched Annex-J curves). The remaining encode-time quality objective is a SSIMULACRA2 score floor, not a butteraugli-anchored quality mapping: see lege-ecosystem.work.jp2lam-ssim-controller and lege-ecosystem.decision.jp2lam-ssim-canonical-metric. Grade screens with the pinned in-tree metric; keep butteraugli as a reported secondary column only.

### Decide whether a native-text-only OCR job may run without an available OCR backend

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem.work.document-ocr-cli-native-text-backend-init/1`

cargo test -p lege-document-ocr-cli fails on any non-Windows host, and it is the one unsatisfied
acceptance check on the Business-grade PDF OCR CLI milestone.

WHAT HAPPENS: tests::native_text_batch_exports_and_resumes_without_invoking_ocr builds a PDF with
a real text layer and runs the batch with BackendArg::WinocrLegacy, deliberately choosing a
backend that is unavailable so that reaching OCR at all would fail loudly. But
DocumentProcessor::new initializes the backend eagerly
(lege-document-ocr/crates/pipeline/src/lib.rs:129-133, initialize_backend at line 1018), so
construction returns UnavailableBackend("winocr-legacy") before any page is classified and
run_batch panics at lege-document-ocr/cli/src/main.rs:849. The test was added in 27900f0e, after
b6c6ae48 made initialization eager, so it has never passed off Windows.

WHY THIS IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX, AND WHAT THE NEXT SESSION MUST DECIDE. There is a product
question underneath the failing test: should a document whose pages all carry a native text layer
require a working OCR backend at all? Three answers, and they are not equivalent:

(a) Keep eager initialization and mark the test #[cfg(target_os = "windows")]. Smallest diff.
Costs the assertion on Linux, where it becomes vacuous, and leaves the underlying behaviour
(a text-only job refusing to start on a host with no OCR backend) in place.

(b) Make backend initialization lazy, so the error surfaces only when a page actually needs OCR.
This is what the test's name asserts and what the vestigial DocumentProcessor::backend() ->
Result signature at lib.rs:180 was shaped for. The obstacle is that new() also uses the resolved
backend to rewrite config.backend, config.tensorrt_paddle, the model identity and the selection
warning; config.backend then feeds configuration_hash(), which is the resume/checkpoint identity.
Deferring initialization means the recorded backend is the requested one rather than the resolved
one, which silently changes when a resumed job is considered to have the same configuration. That
seam has to be designed, not patched.

(c) Keep eager initialization but let it degrade: construct successfully with no backend, record
the reason, and fail only at the point of use. Same checkpoint-identity question as (b), plus
selected_backend_name() and the Debug impl need a defined answer when there is no backend.

Nothing here is urgent -- the shipped Windows path is unaffected -- but the milestone cannot be
completed until it is settled, and the check is left deliberately unsatisfied rather than
weakened.

### Emit printed text as an embedded per-document glyph font (text_format glyphfont)

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem.work.glyph-font-text-output/1`

Replace the JBIG2/CCITT raster text layer with a PDF text object drawn from one document-wide TrueType font whose glyphs are clustered connected components of the binarized pages. Staged: (1) pixel-exact staircase outlines, first-seen prototypes, incremental document-wide dictionary, writer emits the font at finalize under a reserved id; (2) font-oriented clustering: majority-vote prototypes, edge-tolerant structural matching, alias merging into TrueType composites, page-median descent and advance; (3) quadratic Bezier outlines fitted to the prototypes with a raster-back check and staircase fallback; (4) ToUnicode by aligning glyph placements to OCR words, replacing the invisible OCR layer on glyph pages; (5) text orientation and skew straightening from the components themselves, and deduplication under the printing-press prior (a book has one piece of type per letter, so like shapes inked differently are one glyph); (6) text at any angle, the same orientation measurement turning pages upright for OCR in every text format, and a matching path fast enough not to matter (no rayon; word-parallel kernels); (7) the rest of the page's cost at the raised render height: the renderer's fast paths for gray scans, the preserved mask's coverage plane, and the background encoded at the height the caller asked for.

### Handoff: remaining `jp2lam` JPEG 2000 decode gaps

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem.work.handoff-remaining-jp2lam-jpeg-2000-decode-gaps/1`

**Audience:** an agent continuing the JPX decode work in `jp2lam`.
**Context:** `jp2lam` is the JPEG 2000 codec behind the `pdf-renderer` port of
PDFium. Its decoder feeds `/JPXDecode` images. A differential sweep of
`pdf-renderer` against PDFium found ~610 corpus pages rendering **blank**
because their JPX image failed to decode and the error was swallowed. That has
been root-caused and mostly fixed; this document hands off the residual tail.

### jp2lam decoder optimisation: the remaining tail

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem.work.jp2lam-jpeg-2000-decoder-optimization-plan/1`

The single live record for the jp2lam JPEG 2000 decoder optimisation effort. It
replaces the ~125 work records the 2026-08 bulk import created from the five
planning documents in lege-codecs/jp2lam/decode-fix-plan/; those were abandoned on
2026-09-08 as mis-imported markdown headings. The documents themselves stay on disk
and remain the detailed authority.

Status re-verified against lege-codecs/jp2lam/src on 2026-09-08 (repo HEAD 823d46dd).

LANDED, confirmed in current source:
- Jp2DecodeStats stage attribution (src/decode/stats.rs).
- Renderer-oriented decode API: DecodeRequest / DecodeResolution / DecodeOutputFormat /
  Jp2Decoder, plus decode_into() writing straight into caller memory (src/decode/mod.rs).
- Reduced-resolution decode, including multi-tile (select_reduce_levels,
  reduced_axis_bounds in src/decode/mod.rs).
- Tier-1-fused dequantization with no separate full coefficient plane
  (src/decode/reconstruct.rs, src/decode/t1.rs).
- Fused packed output with byte-identity tests, and a direct sYCC 4:2:0 kernel
  (reconstruct_fused_packed_into in src/decode/reconstruct.rs).
- Banded vertical 9/7 reconstruction at VERTICAL_BAND_COLS = 128 and coarse-chunk
  horizontal scratch (src/dwt/irrev97.rs).
- Lattice-aligned nonzero tile-origin routing into the optimized inverse DWT
  (lattice_aligned_origin in src/decode/reconstruct.rs).
- Weighted largest-processing-time Tier-1 scheduling over a shared work cursor with
  one persistent Tier1Scratch per pool worker (decode_codeblocks_parallel in
  src/decode/t1.rs), bit-exact against the serial path.
- Tier-2 allocation hygiene: range-based precinct block membership, streaming
  PacketStats instead of retained packet records, try_reserve from header-derived
  counts (src/decode/t2.rs).
- Renderer integration: thread-local persistent Jp2Decoder, DecodeConcurrency::Budgeted,
  DecodeResolution::AtLeast from the device footprint
  (lege-pdf/render/crates/pdf-image/src/jpx.rs).
- All four correctness classes of HANDOFF-remaining-jpx-decode.md (precincts/SOP/EPH,
  degenerate 1-sample DWT, zero-length contribution for the named repros, TPsot==TNsot
  tail) were resolved before the 2026-08-05 audit was written.

NEGATIVE RESULT, do not re-land as-is: the wide f32x8 fused ICT/clamp/interleave SIMD
experiment (commit c2c8dbf1) was performance-neutral and byte-identical because fat-LTO
LLVM already vectorizes the scalar loop; the stage is memory-bandwidth-bound.

GENUINELY OPEN, in the order the plan itself recommends:
1. True windowed / line-based ROI decode (plan Milestone 8, audit section 10,
   NEXT-audit-phases Phase 5). Today ROI runs the full inverse DWT per tile and clips
   while packing; see the comment at src/decode/mod.rs around line 421. The interim
   region-sized destination allocation landed, the windowed subband IDWT with halo did
   not.
2. Tier-2 cleanups: the merged-block HashMap<(usize,usize), MergedBlock> at
   src/decode/t2.rs:268 is still a HashMap rather than a dense index, and
   build_packet_positions still eagerly sorts packet positions instead of iterating a
   progression order.
3. Tier-1 style specialization, compact FlagGrid words and stripe-major coefficient
   layout (plan sections 20-24). Only the stripe_is_clean fast path exists
   (src/tier1/flags.rs).
4. Architecture-specific SIMD and PGO (plan Milestone 5 remainder,
   NEXT-audit-phases Phase 6). src/simd/x86/mod.rs still carries an empty AVX2 shell:
   "No AVX2 overrides are installed." No PGO build configuration and no GPU backend.
5. Small renderer follow-ups: Rgbx8/Bgra8 exist in the codec but jpx.rs maps only
   Gray8/GrayA8/Rgb8/Rgba8/Cmyk8, so a 4-byte-pixel GPU compositing path still swizzles.
6. sYCC 4:2:2 and 4:4:4 direct kernels (only 4:2:0 landed).
7. Tile-part QCC component quantization override is still rejected outright
   (MARKER_QCC in src/j2k/decode_markers.rs), one of the post-precinct census residuals.

WHAT THE NEXT SESSION MUST DECIDE FIRST: item 1 and item 4 are the two the plan itself
called the hardest and deferred, and both are profiling-gated. The detailed
DWT/Tier-1/final-pack flamegraph predates the 128-column vertical band and the
direct-output change, so refresh stage attribution with the current decode_benchmark
before picking any hot-loop target. Items 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 are independently landable
without that.

### jp2lam SSIMULACRA2 score-floor quality controller

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem.work.jp2lam-ssim-controller/1`

Give jp2lam a SSIMULACRA2 score-floor quality controller: the smallest exact stream, within a bounded probe budget, whose reconstructed pixels meet a requested minimum score. Share JPXL's pinned production metric (`ssimulacra2-jpxl-1` in jpxl-perceptual) rather than a second implementation. Port JPXL controller mathematics (log-loss crossing, geometric bracket, work budgets, refuse-under-target) into a JPEG 2000-native two-dimensional search: outer global quantizer scale, inner PCRD body-bytes truncation over stored Tier-1 passes. Keep existing perceptual PCRD as the local allocator. Do not port the JPXL predictor, quantizer ladder, or structure-reuse rules. Do not change RateControl::Quality(u8) semantics until a later mapping session. v1 is Sessions 1-5 of the 2026-09-04 implementation plan (shared metric, Perceptual API, slow evaluator, PCRD-only proof, outer QuantRung).

### Preservation mode: an MRC document beside the e-ink preparation mode

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem.work.preservation-mode/1`

Give Lege a second top-level mode. Preparation, everything it does today, rebuilds a book for an e-ink screen: binarize, dither, drop the colour, re-encode at the device's height. Preservation would keep the book as it is — no binarization of the page, no colour touched — and compress it as layers instead: a JPEG 2000 background under a crisp JBIG2 ink layer (or the DjVu equivalent, IW44 under JB2), at a requested resolution, with hOCR still running and truetyping available as an opt-in. The plan is written; nothing is implemented.

### 3. Zero-length code-block contribution (truncated streams) — ~6 files

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem.work.zero-length-code-block-contribution-truncated/1`

- **Error:** `non-empty code-block contribution has zero byte length`
- **Repro:** was seen on `Stalin…` (that hit is an `.epub`, not a PDF — find a
  PDF trigger by re-running the census with `JPXDUMPDIR` set and grabbing the
  dumped `failjpx_…zerobytelength….jp2`).
- **Reject site:** `src/decode/t2.rs` ~line 481-485, in the packet-header
  contribution reader: a code-block signals inclusion but decodes a body length
  of 0, which the code treats as malformed.
- **Diagnosis:** these are **truncated** streams (the file is cut off; the
  packet header promises data the body doesn't contain). PDFium/OpenJPEG salvage
  the partial image (they render what decoded). `jp2lam` errors → blank.
- **Recommended approach (careful — correctness risk):** treat a truncated tail
  as *end of data*, not a hard error: stop Tier-2 at the first packet that runs
  past the available bytes, keep the coefficients decoded so far, and let
  reconstruction produce the partial image (this mirrors how `pdf-structure`
  already salvages truncated Flate content streams). The catch is that the
  reconstruct path currently expects a complete packet sequence (`finish()` at
  t2.rs ~line 225 errors on `ended early`). You'll need reconstruct to tolerate
  missing contributions (zero-fill those code-blocks). **Verify the partial
  output matches OpenJPEG's partial output**, not just "it doesn't error" — a
  partial decode that diverges from OpenJPEG is a silent quality regression.
- **Priority:** lower than §1 — truncation is inherently lossy and rare.
